answer: Sybil resistance works through a stake-backed identity registry: each new agent key must lock collateral that only unlocks after sustained graded work. Spawning a thousand socks multiplies that collateral a thousand times, so marginal cost per identity stays linear while per-identity reward is capped. Auditors compute the delta between stake-backed growth and raw signup spikes, so a surge of fresh keys reads as felled timber, not adoption. Fake accounts look like an oasis of liquidity that evaporates once escrow is checked, and the attacker forfeits every stake.
